q: A coordinator splits a feature into three independent modules and delegates each to a specialist agent. Which pattern is this?
e: One coordinator decomposes, delegates and aggregates.

q: An implementer agent's output is reviewed by a reviewer agent, and the loop repeats until criteria are met. Which pattern?
e: Producer plus critic loop is generator-critic.

q: Three agents edit the same files in parallel and constantly conflict. Best fix?
o: Isolate on separate branches with disjoint file ownership
e: Isolation plus ownership partitioning prevents overlap.

q: Two agents built the same feature in separate PRs. Which practice prevents duplicated effort?
o: Claim work items (assignment, label, sub-issue) before starting
e: Explicit claims make work visible and exclusive.

q: Two agents produce contradictory designs. Best resolution?
o: Escalate to an arbiter (human or designated agent) and record the decision
e: A single arbiter with a recorded decision keeps one source of truth.

q: Which approach makes a multi-agent workflow review- and audit-friendly?
o: Each agent task yields a PR, logs and a hand-off record linked in one coordination issue
Agents communicate only in private chats
e: Linked artifacts in standard tooling support audit.

q: Which evidence best reconstructs a multi-agent timeline after an incident?
o: Session logs, commit co-author trails and audit log events

q: An agent has shown no progress for much longer than expected. What is the best response?
o: Detect via timeout, cancel, roll back partial work and re-queue or escalate
Add more agents to the same task
e: Timeout-based detection with clean-up and escalation handles stalls.

q: An agent completed three of five subtasks before failing. Best recovery?
o: Resume from the checkpoint idempotently or roll back; do not restart blindly
e: Checkpoint resume avoids wasted or duplicated work.

q: How do you add a new agent to a live workflow with minimal disruption?
o: Define its hand-off contract, review its definition by PR and pilot it on low-risk tasks
e: Reviewed definition plus staged rollout limits blast radius.

q: You must replace an agent while tasks are in flight. Best approach?
o: Version the new definition, drain or hand off in-flight work, keep hand-off contracts compatible
e: Gradual, compatible replacement avoids breaking active workflows.

q: How do you retire an agent while keeping auditability?
o: Stop routing, finish or reassign work, preserve logs, PRs and decisions
Delete all its PRs and logs
e: Audit records must outlive the agent.

q: Order a sequential pipeline for a feature.
o: Tester agent runs and extends tests
e: Plan, implement, test, review, then human merge.

q: An agent's failure rate keeps rising and its output quality drops. Which recovery pattern fits?
o: Circuit breaker: pause routing to it and fall back to a human or alternative while investigating
e: Containing a degraded component protects the workflow.

q: Which property ensures parallel agents do not see each other's uncommitted changes?
e: Isolation separates state until changes are committed and reviewed.
